name: Airway Infantile Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnostic Criteria for Airway Infantile Hemangioma

criteria.description: Presence of biphasic stridor or respiratory distress in infants typically aged 1-6 months
Endoscopic visualization of a subglottic or airway vascular lesion consistent with hemangioma
MRI or CT showing a well-circumscribed, enhancing soft tissue mass in the subglottic airway
Clinical improvement with beta-blocker therapy supportive of diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical presentation plus endoscopic visualization of airway hemangioma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by endoscopy and imaging; biopsy is rarely needed due to bleeding risk.

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine labs typically normal
imaging: MRI showing well-defined, intensely enhancing subglottic mass
CT scan demonstrating airway narrowing with soft tissue lesion
Ultrasound of neck may show characteristic hemangioma features
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; sporadic occurrence
other: Endoscopic visualization of a red to purple vascular lesion in the subglottic airway

distinguishingFeatures: Inspiratory stridor without a discrete mass
Fixed airway narrowing without vascular lesion
Different imaging characteristics (slow flow vs. proliferative)
No typical infantile hemangioma growth pattern

redFlags: Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
Stridor at rest or with minimal exertion
references: Mulliken JB, Glowacki J. Hemangiomas and vascular malformations in infants and children: a classification based on endothelial characteristics. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1982 Mar;69(3):412-22.
Haggstrom AN, Drolet BA, Baselga E, et al. Prospective study of infantile hemangiomas: clinical characteristics predicting complications and treatment. Pediatrics. 2006;118(3):882-887.
Bruckner AL, Frieden IJ. Hemangiomas of infancy. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2003;48(4):477-493.
